Introducing Grok Bot

_[Blog](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot) · [Docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview) · [Get started](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/get-started)_

* * *

Today we’re launching **Grok Bot** in early beta: AI teammates you can give real work to.
Bots sign in to the tools you already use and work in them just like you do, on a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal. They finish jobs end to end and only come back when something needs your approval.

You work with a Bot like you would a teammate. Give it a task, shut your computer, and pick the thread back up from desktop or iOS.

[Introducing Grok Bot](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F1_0Lkp16Rc "Introducing Grok Bot")

**What’s new:**

* **A computer of its own:** Bots work on a persistent cloud computer that keeps their files and logins, with connectors and MCP where available, and computer use everywhere else, so work lands in the real tool, not a draft you have to move.
* **Bots that coordinate with each other:** Your Bots share one computer, and each gets its own screen, so several can work in parallel. They message each other, share context in threads and group chats, and pass ownership between themselves.
* **Show a Bot how it’s done:** Ask a Bot to follow along once through a multi-step path across your systems. It saves that path as a routine and re-runs it on demand or on a schedule.

The computer is isolated to your account rather than to an individual Bot, so treat a login or file placed on it as available to all of your Bots. [Approvals, security, and privacy](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy) has more details.

Grok Bot is in beta and available today on **desktop** and **iOS** for **SuperGrok Heavy** , **Cursor Ultra** , and **Cursor Teams Premium** subscribers. Enterprise users can [join the waitlist](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot) for future access. Download the app and create your first teammate.

We’d love to hear what you hand off to your first Bot. If you hit an issue, please email [hi@cursor.com](mailto:hi@cursor.com) or post in [Bug Reports](https://forum.cursor.com/c/support/bug-report/6) , so we can track and address it properly.

# Grok Bot Runs on Cursor's Infrastructure, Not SpaceXAI's

SpaceXAI's new AI teammate app launched today, but its downloads, pricing, and checkout still run entirely through Cursor.

Roo's Newsletter

[Roo's Newsletter](https://roo.beehiiv.com/authors/roo-s-newsletter)

Aug 11, 2026

•

5 min read

Quick recommendation before the Article: if you want a Life Planner Notion Template system, the [_All-in-One Notion Life Planner_](https://yulianashub.gumroad.com/l/all-in-one-notion-life-planner?utm_source=roo.beehiiv.com&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=notion-university-template-the-ones-worth-duplicating-checked-against-real-ratings&_bhlid=2f2f3efe4cf298fea0d65ac239a927c493a18513) is worth starting with.
SpaceXAI launched Grok Bot today, its first general-purpose AI agent product, pitched as a team of always-on AI teammates that sign into your tools and finish real work. But open the checkout flow on SpaceXAI's own page and something doesn't match the branding: every download link, every pricing button, and both paid plan names belong to Cursor, not Grok. Grok Bot is a SpaceXAI product running on Cursor's infrastructure, weeks before the two companies' $60 billion merger has even been confirmed closed.

### What Grok Bot actually is

Grok Bot gives each user one or more AI agents that operate their own cloud computer, sign into the apps and websites a person already uses, and keep working after that person's laptop is closed. You message a Bot the way you'd text a coworker, and it either finishes the job or comes back only when it needs approval.
Bots have their own computer and sign into the tools you already use, and they finish jobs end to end, only coming back when something needs your approval.

The pitch is that Grok Bot skips the setup step most agent tools require. Rather than asking a user to build workflows and routines first, Grok Bot is meant to just get a task done once you message it. A bot can also learn by watching: the best way for a Bot to learn a workflow is to have it follow along the next time a person does the job, after which it saves the steps as a routine and runs it on its own.

Multiple bots can run at once, with one acting as a coordinator over specialist bots for different lanes of work, and they can pass tasks between each other in shared threads without a human relaying notes.
SpaceXAI describes bots researching sales prospects, drafting outreach, updating CRM records, processing invoices from Gmail, preparing marketing campaigns, reproducing bugs, and managing support queues, examples pulled directly from how the product was used inside the company before release. [xAI](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot)

### The infrastructure tells a different story than the branding

The macOS, Windows, and Linux installers are hosted at `downloads.cursor.com` . The enterprise contact form is `cursor.com/contact-sales` . And the two subscription tiers you can actually buy aren't named after Grok at all — they're called **Cursor Ultra** and **Cursor Premium Teams** , priced the same as Cursor's existing developer plans. SpaceXAI is selling a Grok-branded product through a Cursor-branded checkout.

This lines up with reporting from before the launch.
Tech publications reported that a general-purpose agent product developed at Cursor under the internal codename "Sand" was slated for rebranding as "Grok Bot," and that Cursor's own brand name would be gradually phased out over the coming months as the two companies integrate. Grok Bot appears to be that product, shipped under a new name while its plumbing, from download servers to sales contact forms to plan pricing, is still entirely Cursor's.

The App Store listing adds a second data point pointing the same direction. According to independent reporting on the launch, the iOS app is listed with Anysphere, Cursor's parent company, as the developer, while the desktop downloads and sales links are hosted by Cursor — even though the product is marketed under the Grok name on SpaceXAI's site.

### Why the merger timing matters here

None of this is happening in a vacuum.
SpaceX agreed on June 16 to acquire Anysphere, the developer of Cursor, for $60 billion in stock after the two companies began sharing compute and jointly training AI models, with the transaction expected to close in the third quarter. As of this week, that deal had not formally closed. One financial outlet reported the acquisition could close as early as the following weekend and no later than the end of August, pending final regulatory approval.

So Grok Bot went live to the public running on the acquirer-to-be's infrastructure while the acquisition itself is still pending. That's not unusual for two companies that have been operationally intertwined for months. Cursor and SpaceXAI jointly trained Grok 4.5, which Cursor introduced in July as its first model built for knowledge work outside software engineering, and Grok Bot packages that model strategy into a standalone worker with persistent access to a computer rather than limiting it to a chat window or code editor. Grok 4.
5 itself launched July 8 as the two companies' first jointly developed model, positioned as a coding and agentic-work tool that Musk described as an 'Opus-class' model, referencing what was until recently Anthropic's top model family.

Put the three data points together (the branding, the codename leak, and the checkout infrastructure) and the picture is a company operating as one entity in production before the paperwork says it's one entity.

### Pricing and availability

There's no single page that lays out the full Grok Bot access grid, so here's the merged version, pulled from SpaceXAI's own pricing section and cross-checked against the launch coverage.

|Access path |Price |What you get |Platforms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|SuperGrok Heavy subscription |Included in existing plan |Grok Bot access via current subscription, no new purchase |Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux), iOS |
|Cursor Ultra |$200/month, billed monthly |Grok Bot's own cloud computer, tool sign-in, scheduled routines, extended AI token limits |Desktop, iOS |
|Cursor Premium Teams |$120/seat/month, billed monthly |Everything in Ultra, plus centralized team billing, a team marketplace for skills/plugins, shared usage analytics, and SAML/OIDC SSO |Desktop, iOS |
|Enterprise |Not listed, waitlist only |Unspecified, contact sales |Waitlist |

SpaceXAI announced the release of Grok Bot on Tuesday as an AI tool designed to complete work tasks independently across multiple applications, operating on its own cloud-based computer and returning to users only when approval is needed. Grok Bot launched in beta on Mac and iOS, with Windows and Linux desktop versions also available and Android listed as coming soon; access is initially restricted to SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium subscribers.

### The trust question nobody in the launch materials answers directly

...

Anysphere's App Store disclosure states the iOS app may collect data linked to a user's identity, including contact information, user content, identifiers, usage data, and diagnostics, though Apple notes those privacy declarations are supplied by the developer and are not independently verified. Cursor's broader platform offers a privacy mode and security assessments, and prevents code data from being used for training when that mode is enabled, but Grok Bot's own launch materials put the immediate emphasis on user approvals and learned routines rather than a detailed data policy.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is Grok Bot the same thing as the "Sand" project reported earlier this month?**  
It's not confirmed by name, but the timing and description match closely.
A general-purpose agent product developed at Cursor under the codename "Sand" was reported to be headed for a Grok Bot rebrand as part of the wider phase-out of the Cursor name, and Grok Bot's description as a cloud-agent product line built on Cursor's technology fits that reporting.

**Has the SpaceX-Cursor acquisition officially closed?**  
Not as of this launch. The $60 billion stock acquisition was agreed on June 16 with a close expected in the third quarter, and separate reporting placed the likely close date within weeks of early August, pending regulatory approval.

**Why does a Grok-branded product use Cursor's download servers and plan names?**  
SpaceXAI hasn't explained this directly. The most consistent explanation, based on the pending-acquisition timeline and the "Sand" codename reporting, is that the two companies are already running shared infrastructure and simply haven't rebuilt Grok-branded billing and hosting yet.
**What does Grok Bot cost if I'm not already a SuperGrok Heavy subscriber?**  
$200 a month for an individual Cursor Ultra plan, or $120 per seat per month for Cursor Premium Teams, both billed monthly. Enterprise pricing isn't published; those customers go on a waitlist.

**Can Grok Bot use apps that don't have an API?**  
Yes. An agent can navigate websites that lack an API or Model Context Protocol connection, giving it a wider theoretical range than workflow tools that require a supported integration, though that also exposes it to the same changing interfaces and permission boundaries that make browser automation difficult.

Set up Grok Bot, create your first Bot, and hand it a useful task.

## Before you begin

You need:

* An eligible plan: SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, Cursor Teams Premium
* The Grok Bot desktop app for macOS or Windows
* An app or website where your first Bot can do useful work

Grok Bot is not currently available as a Linux desktop app. You can also set up and use Grok Bot for iOS .

> Grok Bot requires cloud data storage. Accounts using Legacy Privacy Mode
> must move to a supported Cursor data setting before Grok Bot can start.
Open [Cursor privacy settings](https://cursor.com/dashboard/settings?openPrivacy=true) to review the account setting.
> 
> 

## 1\. Install the desktop app

Open the [Grok Bot access page](https://cursor.com/bot/onboarding) and choose
the download for your computer.

### macOS

1. Choose the Apple silicon or Intel download.
2. Open the downloaded disk image.
3. Drag **Grok Bot** to **Applications** .
4. Open Grok Bot. If macOS asks for confirmation, choose **Open** .

To check which download you need, open **Apple menu → About This Mac** . A **Chip** field means Apple silicon; a **Processor** field means Intel.

### Windows

1. Choose the x64 or Arm64 download.
2. Run the installer.
3. Open Grok Bot from the Start menu.

To check the architecture, open **Settings → System → About → System type** .

Grok Bot checks for updates automatically. You can also use **Check for Updates** from **Settings → Beta** .

## 2\. Sign in

1. Choose **Get started** on the welcome screen.
If you are already in the app,
2. Finish authentication in the browser window that opens.
3. Return to Grok Bot after the browser confirms the sign-in.

Grok Bot uses your Cursor account. If your organization requires single sign-on
(SSO), complete the normal organization sign-in flow.

On first use, Grok Bot introduces Bots, the shared computer, and routines, then
asks which tools you use. These answers shape the first teammate suggestions;
they do not connect or modify those tools by themselves. Computer setup runs in
the background and the final step opens **Meet a future teammate** .

## 3\. Create your first Bot

Choose a suggested teammate from **Meet a future teammate** , or choose **Create your own** and give the Bot:

* A short name
* One primary job
* A description of how it should work

For example:

> **Name:** Piper  
> **Job:** Product performance  
> **Description:** Investigate product-performance questions using our
> observability tools.

...

Then try a task in one of your tools:

> Open our analytics dashboard and compare new-user activation for this week
> with the previous four weeks. Identify the largest step-level change and
> draft a short investigation plan with links to the relevant charts. Do not
> change any dashboards. Ask me to sign in if needed.
> 
> 

Before allowing external changes, review Approvals, security, and privacy .

When the Bot reaches an app that requires authentication, it may ask you to
take over the computer.

1. Open **Agent Computer** from the conversation.
2. Choose the takeover control.
3. Enter the password, passkey, two-factor code, or complete the CAPTCHA
   yourself.
4. Return control to the Bot.

The browser session persists on your shared Grok Bot computer, so other Bots
can use the same signed-in session when appropriate.

For supported services, you can also install a connector from **Settings → Plugins** and authenticate it in your browser.
